newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY - SABRES SLAM KINGS 6-2.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY - SABRES SLAM KINGS 6-2.

text.p: Brian Holzinger and Derek Plante each had two goals and an assist and Dominik Hasek turned aside 37 shots to help the Buffalo Sabres to a 6-2 victory over the slumping Los Angeles Kings on Friday.
Matthew Barnaby and Donald Audette added a goal and an assist apiece for Buffalo, which has won four of its last five games.
The Sabres scored three goals in the final 2:32, including two by Plante, who has scored 14 of his 16 goals at home this season.

"There are certain players that have a natural instinct how to fire up a team, Matthew Barnaby is definitely one of those," Sabres coach Ted Nolan said. "He took it upon himself to get something going."
Ray Ferraro and John Slaney tallied for the Kings.

In Chicago, Mark Fitzpatrick made 34 saves and Scott Mellanby had a pair of power-play goals and an assist as the Florida Panthers snapped a four-game road losing streak by shutting down the sputtering Chicago Blackhawks, 3-1.
Radek Dvorak added a goal and an assist for Florida, which won for just the second in six games.
Sergei Krivokrasov scored the only goal for Chicago.

In Hartford, Arturs Irbe stopped 30 shots for his first win in nearly a month and Dave Reid had a goal and an assist, leading the Dallas Stars to a 4-1 victory over the Hartford Whalers that extended their unbeaten streak to six games.
Former Whaler Pat Verbeek had three assists for the Stars.

Irbe made 22 saves over the final two periods, including a sliding pad stop on Andrew Cassels' redirection in the second. He also used his blocker and stick to stop Keith Primeau, who was all alone in front of the net midway through the first period.

In Phoenix, Keith Tkachuk scored twice and Jeremy Roenick and Craig Janney each added a goal and an assist as the Phoenix Coyotes topped the Toronto Maple Leafs, 5-2 for their season-high fourth straight victory.
Jim McKenzie also scored and Dallas Drake had two assists for the Coyotes, who have won eight of their last 11 games to vault into third place in the Central Division.
Jamie Baker and Todd Warriner tallied for Toronto, which has dropped four of its last five games and leads the league with 21 losses.
In Washington, Phil Housley's goal with 2:27 left in third period lifted the Washington Capitals to a 3-2 victory over the San Jose Sharks, ending a seven-game winless streak.

Dale Hunter was in the right faceoff circle and flipped a pass to Housley, who was streaking down the slot. He fired a backhander into the top right corner of the net that appeared to catch goaltender Chris Terreri off-guard.
"I think it was a surprise beacuse I came off the bench," said Housley. "Coming off the bench, you sort of watch the play ahead of you and their guys just never saw me coming off the bench."
Sergei Gonchar scored twice for the Capitals.
In Edmonton, Scott Stevens' goal with 6:46 remaining, his first since March 30th, gave the New Jersey Devils their club-record fifth straight road win, 3-2 over the slumping Edmonton Oilers.

The Devils improved to 5-0-1 in their last six games after an apparent tying goal by Doug Weight with 16.4 seconds to go was nullified by a goaltender interference penalty on Edmonton's Ryan Smyth. Smyth knocked goaltender Martin Brodeur down and kept him pinned to the ice as Weight whipped a short wrister into an open net.
Jason Arnott scored the other goal for Edmonton.

In Vancouver, Martin Gelinas scored the eventual game-winner 99 seconds into the third period and Corey Hirsch made 30 saves as the Vancouver Canucks snapped a seven-game home winless streak against the Detroit Red Wings with a 3-2 victory.
Adrian Aucoin and Lonny Bohonos also scored for the Canucks. Viacheslav Fetisov and Steve Yzerman tallied for the Red Wings.

In Anaheim, Guy Hebert turned aside 39 shots for his third shutout of the season and Joe Sacco and Paul Kariya each scored twice as the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim used a team-record three shorthanded goals to blank the Calgary Flames, 7-0.
The win was the Ducks' third in six games (3-2-1) and ended Calgary's three-game winning streak.
